<explanation>
Based on the file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a system design diagram for the PureScript compiler project. This is a compiler that transforms PureScript code into JavaScript, written in Haskell.

1. Main Components:
   The diagram should include these key components:

   a. Frontend Components:
   - Parser/Lexer (src/Language/PureScript/CST/)
   - Type Checker (src/Language/PureScript/TypeChecker/)
   - Syntax Sugar Desugaring (src/Language/PureScript/Sugar/)

   b. Core Components:
   - CoreFn IR (src/Language/PureScript/CoreFn/)
   - CoreImp IR (src/Language/PureScript/CoreImp/)
   - Optimizer (src/Language/PureScript/CoreImp/Optimizer/)

   c. Backend Components:
   - JavaScript Code Generator (src/Language/PureScript/CodeGen/JS/)
   - Source Map Generation

   d. Development Tools:
   - IDE Support (psc-ide/)
   - REPL (src/Language/PureScript/Interactive/)
   - Documentation Generator (src/Language/PureScript/Docs/)

2. Component Relationships:
   Show the compilation pipeline with directional arrows:

   ```
   Source Code → CST → TypeChecked AST → CoreFn → CoreImp → JavaScript
   ```

   Use different colors/shapes to distinguish:
   - Input/Output artifacts (rectangles)
   - Processing stages (rounded rectangles)
   - Optimization passes (hexagons)
   - Supporting tools (ovals)

3. Detailed Elements:

   a. For each major component, include:
   - Input/output formats
   - Key transformations performed
   - Important optimizations
   - External dependencies

   b. Show parallel processes:
   - Module system handling
   - Type checking
   - Documentation generation

4. Supporting Systems:
   Include auxiliary components:
   - Build system integration
   - Package management
   - Foreign Function Interface (FFI)
   - Source map generation

5. Design Guidelines:

   a. Use a layered approach:
   - Frontend layer (parsing, type checking)
   - Core layer (intermediate representations)
   - Backend layer (code generation)
   - Tools layer (IDE, REPL)

   b. Color coding:
   - Source processing stages (blue)
   - Optimization passes (green)
   - Code generation (orange)
   - Development tools (purple)

   c. Include important cross-cutting concerns:
   - Error reporting system
   - Module system
   - Type system
   - FFI system

6. Implementation Details:
   Show key implementation aspects:
   - Intermediate representations (CoreFn, CoreImp)
   - Optimization passes
   - Type checking phases
   - Code generation strategies

7. External Interfaces:
   Highlight integration points:
   - JavaScript runtime
   - Node.js ecosystem
   - Build tools
   - Editor integration

The diagram should maintain a balance between showing the compiler's complexity while keeping it understandable. Use hierarchical grouping to manage complexity, with the ability to expand sections for more detail.

Label all components clearly and include a legend explaining the symbols and color coding used. Consider creating multiple views (high-level overview, detailed pipeline, tool integration) for different audiences.

This will provide a comprehensive view of the PureScript compiler's architecture while keeping it accessible to developers working on different aspects of the system.
